A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proved the convergence of the loop-erased radial SLE(4) path to chordal SLE (4) in the bulk of a simply connected domain.
loop-erased radial SLE(4) is equivalent to radial SLE (2) and that loop-erasing chordal SLE (2k) is equivalent to chordal SLE(k) for any k>0.
we give a proof of the loop-erased scaling limit conjecture of Schramm.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the scaling limit can be established by a direct argument using the convergence of loop-erase random walk to radial Schramm–Loewner evolution, rather than by the convergence of loop erased random walk to Brownian motion, which was the main approach used by Schramm and Sheffield in [arXiv:0909.4549].
the scaling limit results for loop-erased walk and for radial SLE can be proved by the same method.
Wilson’s algorithm can be used to prove convergence of the loop-erased path to SLE, at least for simply connected domains, without the need for a conformal mapping.
